 Player Stats

 Sidy Cissoko recorded 17 points (5-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder.
 Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori made a change to his starting lineup on Tuesday, replacing Scoot Henderson with Cissoko. While he didn’t shoot well from the field, Sidy finished with a season-high point total and a solid overall stat line in 33 minutes. Henderson played 23 minutes and finished with 11 points, one rebound, four assists and three three-pointers. Cissoko isn’t a must-add, but he’s worth watching, especially with Ja Morant (hamstring) out for a few more weeks. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Chris Youngblood (foot) will not return to Tuesday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Youngblood injured his right foot early in the fourth quarter and has been ruled out for the rest of the night. Sidy Cissoko and Scoot Henderson can absorb the minutes that would have gone to Youngblood, who is sitting on the Trail Blazers’ bench. 
 Sidy Cissoko 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #91 
 Damian Lillard, Sidy Cissoko, Deni Avdija, Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan will start Tuesday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Cissoko steps into the Trail Blazers’ lineup for Scoot Henderson, who has struggled with inconsistency since Ja Morant’s hamstring injury led to his starting. Cissoko may not be a great offensive threat, but he is a solid defender, which should come in handy in this matchup. 
 Scoot Henderson 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #00 
 Scoot Henderson produced 13 points (4-of-10 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs. 
 Unfortunately for fantasy managers who believed a move into the starting lineup would improve Henderson’s value, he hasn’t delivered. Since Ja Morant (hamstring) went down in an October 29 loss to the Grizzlies, Scoot’s category-league value has ranked outside the top-300 in nine-cat formats. Unsurprisingly, Jrue Holiday (11 points, one steal and one three-pointer) has been far more valuable, regardless of league format. Portland plays three games next week, starting with a home back-to-back against the Thunder on Tuesday and Wednesday. 
 Ja Morant 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #1 
 Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori said on Saturday that Ja Morant (hamstring) “may not be out for as long as we thought.” 
 Morant, who suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain during an October 29 loss to the Grizzlies, was to be re-evaluated towards the end of November. However, according to Nori, a doctor in Los Angeles evaluated Morant and gave him a positive outlook on the injury. That’s good news for those rostering the athletic point guard, who was fitting in well with his new teammates at the time of the injury. Scoot Henderson will start until Morant is healthy enough to play. 
 Scoot Henderson 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #00 
 Scoot Henderson tallied 14 points (4-of-11 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, one assist, three steals and one three-pointer in Saturday’s win over the Jazz. 
 As expected, Henderson replaced Ja Morant (hamstring) in the starting lineup on Saturday. Unfortunately, he produced one assist and four turnovers in 31 minutes, but his steals tally was solid. Jrue Holiday (14/4/3/1 with two three-pointers) played nine fewer minutes than Henderson and was the more efficient of the two. Henderson is worth rostering while Morant sits, but those who add him will likely have to accept the efficiency issues. 
 Ja Morant 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #1 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Ja Morant has been diagnosed with a Grade 2 left hamstring strain and will miss at least four weeks. 
 Morant sustained the injury on Thursday against his former team, and it will cost him the next month, at minimum. Scoot Henderson and Jrue Holiday should see the most run in Morant’s absence, but it’s not yet known which of the pair will start alongside Damian Lillard.

 Ja Morant (hamstring) will not return to Thursday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Morant was ruled out more than halfway through the fourth quarter, and they pulled the starters a couple minutes later. This could have been precautionary, but the team should provide more of an update in the coming days. Scoot Henderson and Jrue Holiday should take on more minutes if Morant misses time, with Jrue likely starting.

 Scoot Henderson (ankle) is available for Tuesday’s game against the Lakers. 
 Initially listed as questionable with a sore left ankle, Henderson is good to go. He’ll take on his usual reserve role and back up Ja Morant.

 #00 
 Scoot Henderson (ankle) is questionable for Tuesday’s game against the Lakers. 
 Henderson has come off the bench in each of Portland’s first two games, most recently playing 21 minutes in Friday’s win over the Kings. If he can’t play on Tuesday, Vit Krejčí may get more playing time, as he played just three minutes against Sacramento. 
 Scoot Henderson 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #00 
 Scoot Henderson accounted for 15 points (7-of-14 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Suns. 
 Among the four guards in Portland’s rotation, Henderson (19 minutes) played the least on Wednesday. He played nine of those minutes after halftime, while starters Ja Morant and Damian Lillard and reserve Jrue Holiday (8/4/1/2) logged between seven and nine minutes each. While Henderson having a role won’t be an issue for him, his playing time might be, especially against tougher opponents.

 Ajay Mitchell recorded 14 points (6-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and one steal in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 Mitchell has scored in double figures in five straight and nine of his last 10 games. Injuries that have beset the Thunder this season have created more opportunities for the third-year guard, who is averaging a career-high 18.5 points per game and providing top-100 fantasy value. As long as Mitchell stays healthy, he’s capable of maintaining his current production all season long.

 Jared McCain tallied 21 points (6-of-12 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 After scoring 19 points off the bench in Saturday’s rout of the Wizards, McCain returned to the Thunder starting lineup on Tuesday. Shooting 4-of-7 from beyond the arc, the third-year guard recorded his third 20-point stat line of the season. While he can be inconsistent, McCain is on a bit of a heater, scoring 21, 19 and 21 points in his last three games.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander recorded 26 points (8-of-22 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and one block in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 After playing the entire third quarter, Gilgeous-Alexander did not play at all in the fourth, as Portland managed to pull away. Due to Oklahoma City’s many injuries, the two-time MVP is being asked to do even more heavy lifting on offense. SGA’s field-goal percentage suffered on Tuesday, but that doesn’t do much to change his status as one of the most valuable players to roster in fantasy basketball. Oklahoma City plays Portland again on Wednesday, and the extra rest time he picked up in the fourth quarter on Tuesday could pay dividends for SGA.

 Deni Avdija finished Tuesday’s win over the Thunder with 24 points (8-of-15 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, eight assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
 Avdija and Damian Lillard took over the third quarter of Tuesday’s 123-103 victory, combining to score 22 of the Trail Blazers’ 38 points. The former supplemented his nine points with three rebounds and three assists in the period, and Deni has scored at least 21 points in eight of Portland’s 10 games. The two teams meet again on Wednesday in what could be another big night for Avdija, who finished Tuesday’s win two assists shy of a double-double.

 Damian Lillard amassed 25 points (8-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder.
 Fans got to see “vintage Dame” during the third quarter, with his production helping Portland grab control of the season. Shooting 5-of-6 from the field, Lillard scored 13 points in the third. The final three points came on a 35-footer as time expired, giving Portland a 17-point lead heading into the fourth quarter. Lillard didn’t play in the fourth quarter, and the 24 minutes he did play may ensure he’s available for Wednesday’s rematch.

 Achiuwa had to leave Tuesday’s game with just under eight minutes left in the third quarter with a leg contusion and did not return. His early exit gave Dylan Cardwell (1/12/1/2/2) more playing time, and he logged 29 minutes off the bench.  Zach LaVine recorded 31 points (10-of-16 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, two steals and six three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Magic.
 While fellow Kings veteran Domantas Sabonis went scoreless on Tuesday, LaVine had one of his most productive games of the season. He recorded his second 30-point game of the season, but he had to head to the locker room during the third quarter with an apparent ankle injury. Sacramento doesn’t play again until Friday, so LaVine will have a little time to recover.

 Acuff continues to impress for the Kings, who fell to 1-10 on Tuesday. The rookie guard has scored at least 20 points in nine of Sacramento’s 11 games, and he’s been a first-round player in 12-team leagues over the last two weeks. As long as he keeps the turnovers in check, Acuff will be a highly valuable fantasy option, regardless of league format.
